terms.meaning: a technique that reads text from a scanned or photographed document
a number from 0 to 1 that shows how sure the OCR tool is about a reading
the step of pulling structured details, such as medicine names, out of raw text

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the review card
sections.what: Brings in the React state tool, icons, the card, badge, button, and style helper. Nothing appears on screen from this section.
sections.why: The review card needs these pieces to draw itself and track edits.

sections.name: OCRMedication
sections.title: Shape of one extracted medicine
sections.what: Describes one medicine read from a document: an id, the corrected name, the original name as read, a dosage, a timing, and a confidence score from 0 to 1.
sections.why: Lets the user compare what the computer read with what they corrected.
sections.watch_out: The confidence score is expected to be between 0 and 1, so a value given as a percentage will look wrong.

sections.name: OCRReviewCard (part 1)
sections.title: Showing one extracted medicine for review
sections.what: Displays one medicine that was read from an uploaded document by the text recognition step, with its name, dosage, timing and a confidence percentage. If confidence is under 80 percent, the card gets an amber warning style. If the name was changed, it shows the original name crossed out.
sections.why: The card lets a person see what the software guessed and correct it, because automatic reading can be wrong. Reason for the 80 percent cut-off is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The 0.8 threshold is typed directly into this component, so changing it means editing this file. The card only compares the name with its original name, so it does not detect changes to dosage or timing.

sections.name: OCRReviewCard (part 2)
sections.title: Dosage and timing fields with edit controls
sections.what: Shows the extracted dosage and timing as plain text, or as editable boxes while editing. Also shows the Correct or Save button and a delete button.
sections.why: Likely reason: the text reading from a report can be wrong, so a person can fix dosage and timing before relying on them.
sections.watch_out: The Save button only switches back to view mode here, so whether changes are stored depends on the parent that receives the update calls.

sections.name: OCRReviewCard (part 3)
sections.title: Low-confidence warning banner
sections.what: When the AI was unsure about the reading and the card is not being edited, shows an amber warning asking the user to check the dosages.
sections.why: Likely reason: flags uncertain readings so a person verifies them.
sections.watch_out: Whether this warning shows depends on the isLowConfidence value, which is set in code not shown here.

summary: A card where a user checks and edits the medicine names read from an uploaded prescription by the OCR tool, based on the visible parts of this file.
purpose: Lets the user confirm or correct text that a computer read from a scanned document before it is saved.
why: OCR can make mistakes, so a human check step is useful. The full reason is not visible because only part of the file is in this packet.
how: The visible part defines what one extracted medicine looks like: an id, the corrected name, the original name as read, a dosage, a timing, and a confidence score from 0 to 1. The rest of the file, not included in this packet, draws the editable list and the review actions.
inputs: A list of extracted medicines from the OCR step.
outputs: Not visible in this packet. The card is expected to show the review list and let the user confirm, edit or delete entries.
risks: A low confidence score may be shown as though it is reliable. Edits that are not saved could be lost. Most behavior is outside this packet.
debug: If a medicine name looks wrong, compare the original name with the corrected name. If confidence values look odd, check that they are between 0 and 1. Check the remaining sections for the edit and save behavior.
